technical_and_design_decisions: Reuse the existing Spring XD samples repository structure, build conventions, module patterns, and supported dependency versions rather than introducing a broad framework upgrade.

Implement the Kafka demonstration as composable XD streams and/or modules with business logic separated from transport concerns, showing replayable Kafka input and separate batch and real-time processing paths where practical.
Implement the Sqoop demonstration as batch jobs covering both JDBC-to-HDFS and HDFS-to-JDBC flows, using configurable connection, table, path, delimiter, and job parameters.
Treat the JDBC-to-HDFS requirement in U7 as a separately documented example, while reusing common configuration and sample data conventions from the Sqoop work where possible.
Modify file-sink name handling by adding a nameExpression option that takes precedence when supplied, while preserving the existing default filename-generation behavior for backward compatibility.
Port the Smart Grid demonstration by adapting its integration points to the current samples repository APIs and conventions instead of attempting a line-for-line migration.

Present Storm and Spark Streaming comparisons as implementation-oriented documentation with equivalent concepts, topology or stream definitions, processing stages, deployment assumptions, and notable differences.

Keep generated documentation changes compatible with the repository's existing documentation toolchain, removing obsolete link rewriting and pushGeneratedDocs behavior rather than replacing it with a new publishing system.

Use automated unit tests for parsing, configuration, and filename behavior, supplemented by focused integration or manual verification against representative Kafka, HDFS, JDBC, Sqoop, Storm, and Spark environments.
assumptions: The existing repository, build, sample applications, and Spring XD extension points are available and buildable; no initial repository recovery or major dependency migration is required.
A working local or shared test environment can provide Kafka, HDFS, JDBC, and Sqoop services, with test credentials and sample data available.
Storm and Spark Streaming comparison deliverables are documentation and example cross-reference updates, not new production-grade Storm or Spark runtimes.
The Smart Grid demo source and its s1-2014 implementation are available for inspection, and its external data sources can be mocked or configured for sample execution.
The increment is intended for demonstration and sample use, so operational hardening, high availability, production security review, and performance benchmarking are excluded.
The developer performs implementation, documentation, testing, and repository integration personally; the estimates represent work-hours rather than elapsed calendar time.
U2 and U7 have overlapping JDBC-to-HDFS concepts, so common sample data, configuration, and documentation patterns can be reused, but both requested demonstrations are delivered.
Existing coding, documentation, and review standards are known and do not require creating a new contribution process.
The file sink option can be implemented without changing the public behavior of existing stream definitions that omit nameExpression.

activities.activity_description: Inspect the existing samples repository, build scripts, XD module conventions, stream and batch examples, file sink implementation, documentation generation, and the historical Smart Grid source. Produce the implementation plan and identify reusable components.

Create the Kafka-based XD data pipeline covering log aggregation and analysis, separation of transport from business logic, avoidance of duplicated processing code, lambda-style processing considerations, and reliable Kafka reprocessing. Add configuration, sample data, execution instructions, and representative tests or verification scripts.

Build and package the Sqoop batch sample for JDBC-to-HDFS and HDFS-to-JDBC movement, including job definitions, parameterization, connection configuration, sample schemas and data, error and rerun guidance, and execution documentation.

Create the additional JDBC-to-HDFS sample requested by U7, reusing compatible configuration and data conventions from the Sqoop work while making the example independently understandable and runnable from the samples repository.

Update the Gradle documentation-generation script, remove the pushGeneratedDocs task and related obsolete configuration, eliminate no-longer-needed link rewriting, and verify that documentation generation succeeds with the revised build.

Review the existing Storm and XD examples and write an implementation-focused comparison explaining equivalent processing concepts, topology or stream structure, configuration, deployment, data flow, and differences relevant to field engineers.

Review the existing Spark Streaming and XD examples and produce a corresponding implementation comparison covering processing model, stages, configuration, deployment, data flow, operational assumptions, and migration or mapping considerations.

Port the s1-2014 Smart Grid demonstration into the current Spring XD samples repository, adapt APIs and build configuration, migrate resources and scripts, resolve compatibility issues, add run instructions, and verify the principal demonstration flow.

Implement the alternative nameExpression option for file-sink stream definitions, map it to the complete filename-generator-expression behavior, preserve the existing default behavior, update parsing and validation, and add unit and focused integration tests plus usage documentation.

Run builds and automated tests, validate sample packaging and documentation generation, exercise representative Kafka, JDBC, HDFS, Sqoop, and file-sink scenarios, verify backward compatibility, and resolve defects found during integration testing.

Complete README files, configuration references, diagrams or flow descriptions where useful, navigation/index updates, sample prerequisites, and consistent instructions across all new and ported examples. Integrate changes into the repository's expected layout.
